title: The ferry song
prose: Halfway across, with neither shore much more than a line, the woman at the steering oar starts to sing. It is a counting song: one verse for each island, one for each river behind you, one for each of the people who taught it to her. The two hanging islands get a verse each, as if they were ordinary.

choices.label: Ask her to sing it again
choices.line: She sings it again, slower, so you can write the verses down. There is a verse for a river you have never heard of, between two you have. She shrugs. It was in the song when she learned it.

choices.label: Listen, and watch the islands
choices.line: You listen to the song and watch the islands come up out of the haze, and the boat keeps time with neither.

notes: The sea road to the Aravali, told as the Vedda's river-litany survives in ordinary mouths: a counting song that still names a river nobody can place. Ties the sayings (`saying_remember_the_rivers`) to something a traveller hears rather than reads. Drafted for the owner to rewrite or approve.
